title: MarginChat iPhone composer concepts
status: Design concepts only; not implemented or deployed
recommendation: A: Compact dock, combined with B: Selection actions
sharedBehavior: Long-press and drag document text without automatically opening the keyboard.
Ask AI reveals the compact composer without autofocus.
Tapping the prompt is explicit typing intent and should open a normal textarea keyboard.
Bottom-right keyboard icon explicitly enters document editing when no AI composer is active.
Keep the composer and send action above the actual visible keyboard, using available viewport dimensions.
Collapse selected text to a chip; retain its source range while the prompt has focus.
Keep model, destination, and attachments behind secondary controls.
Grow the prompt to at most three lines before internal scrolling.
After sending, dismiss keyboard to return room to the document.

proposedSpaceBudget.unit: CSS pixels; targets, not measured iOS constants

keyboardFinding.observation: Public bundle still has old onClick-only toggle, blur before flushSync, and focus with preventScroll. Latest local implementation has touchend and synchronous native focus.
keyboardFinding.limitation: Neither generated concepts nor Happy DOM tests verify the iPhone software keyboard. Fresh deployed build must be tested on a real iPhone/PWA.

concepts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Asset type: high-fidelity mobile web app UX concept board for MarginChat, marginchat.com.
Create a polished, realistic flat product design presentation, NOT a wireframe, NOT a photograph. Landscape canvas, approximately 1536 x 1152. Warm charcoal presentation background. Two equally sized iPhone app screenshots side by side, large enough to read, clean rounded device corners, tiny black bezel, no perspective. Heading at top, discreet state captions under phones. Native iOS status bar 9:41 and home indicator. MarginChat PWA standalone mode, no Safari address bar.
Visual language: calm editorial document workspace; near-black #171918 document canvas, slightly lighter #252a28 controls, soft white text, gray secondary text, muted sage/teal #6db99a accents. Modern clean SF-style sans serif UI with readable 16px-equivalent text and 44px-equivalent touch targets. Thin borders, restrained rounded corners, absolutely no rainbow gradients or oversized AI hero. Inspired by the ease of Gemini's mobile prompt, branded only MarginChat.
Same document in both phones. Compact header back chevron, "MarginChat", ellipsis. Document title "Reading notes", small metadata "Personal workspace". Body: "Make room for deeper thinking." then "Keep one useful idea from each article. Revisit your highlights and connect them to what you already know." Followed by two further quiet paragraphs and a short bulleted list. Highlight the sentence "Revisit your highlights and connect them to what you already know." in translucent sage; clear native selection handles in left phone. Keep text naturally typeset.
HARD LAYOUT CONSTRAINTS: Left phone shows reading and text selection with NO software keyboard, the document occupies almost all the screen. Bottom-right has a distinct 44px keyboard icon for explicitly entering document editing. Right phone shows active prompt typing with a realistic dark iOS QWERTY keyboard including suggestions, keys, space, return, globe, dictation, and home area, deliberately occupying the bottom 47–50 PERCENT of the entire phone display. Above the keyboard, the AI UI must occupy only 10–13 percent of the entire phone height (about 88–108 CSS pixels of an 844px screen). The remaining top third of the phone visibly shows document header and selected document text. Do NOT shrink the keyboard to make the UI fit. The composer must touch the keyboard's top edge with an 8px visual gap at most. Never put app controls beneath the keyboard. Do NOT fill the rest of the viewport with a modal. Document stays full contrast, NO dimming backdrop.
Do not add unsupported voice assistant features to the app composer. Native keyboard dictation key is fine. No duplicated large quotation preview, no visible model list, no model brand name, no destination selector row, no separate modal heading, no instructional paragraphs inside the phones. Use real neat text not lorem ipsum. Presentation labels may be outside phones. Maintain believable screen geometry and meticulous alignment.
Heading text exactly: "A  /  Compact dock"
Small subheading: "A familiar prompt, more room for the document"
Left phone: document reading with selected text. At the bottom a very compact rounded dark prompt dock, in its unfocused state, with a small context label "Selected text" and a single row "Ask Margin…" plus sparkle icon. Keep a separate small keyboard-icon control at bottom-right. Typing has not started. Native selection handles visible in document. No keyboard.
Right phone: very compact two-row rounded composer immediately above keyboard. First row: small bordered context chip with quote icon and text "Selected text" plus x; right-aligned ellipsis menu in the same row for secondary controls. Second row: editable text "Explain this simply" with caret and large sage circular upward-arrow send button at the far right. No extra controls row. Two rows together ~100 CSS px. Selection remains softly highlighted in document but no dragging handles during typing. Keyboard below takes almost half the phone.
Below left phone caption exactly: "Select without opening the keyboard"
Below right phone caption exactly: "Tap the prompt to type"
Small bottom board annotation: "Compact context chip · Settings in one menu · Prompt grows to 3 lines"
concepts.refinement: Refine this existing A / Compact dock concept board. Preserve the entire left phone, board heading, branding, colors, fonts and captions. Change only the right phone layout to simulate a TALLER keyboard: the top boundary of the keyboard, including suggestion row, must start EXACTLY at the vertical midpoint of the right phone's inner screen. In this 1448x1086 image that is approximately canvas y=551, continuing through bottom y=975. Move the small composer UP to directly above that line, approximately y=444 through y=550; preserve its same modest 106px height and two rows (Selected text chip + ellipsis above, Explain this simply + send below). Enlarge keyboard row spacing and lower keyboard area to fill y=551–975 with a believable dark iOS keyboard, no extra key rows. Upper right phone: compress the app header and title spacing enough to keep the highlighted selected sentence visible above the composer. Remove some following paragraph text as needed, representing it scrolled out of the visible area. No overlap between selection and composer. Do not shrink the whole phone or shrink the keyboard. This is a UX space-budget correction: HALF display keyboard, small composer, remaining document visible. Preserve all exact labels.

concepts.refinement: Refine this existing B / Selection actions concept board. Preserve entire left phone, board heading, colors, fonts and captions. Change only right phone to simulate a keyboard occupying the BOTTOM HALF of its INNER DISPLAY. In this 1448x1086 image, keyboard top including suggestions should be at canvas y=545, bottom y=965. Composer should move upward to y=445–544, remaining just 100px tall with Selected text + overflow row and Make this more concise + send row. Enlarge believable native dark iOS keyboard vertical key spacing and bottom area to fill the bottom half, no extra rows. Compress upper header/title gaps and remove lower paragraph content from view to preserve highlighted sentence above composer. While prompt field is focused in the right phone, retain the sage selection highlight but REMOVE the green drag handles, which belong only in left phone selecting mode. No dimming. Preserve all branding and labels. Absolutely don't place keyboard top down at 60 percent like the input image.
